layers.description: The Python forecasting engine, world-model code, adapters, feeds, and local runtime artifacts that drive the core product logic.

layers.name: Surfaces
layers.description: User-facing product surfaces and dashboards across the cockpit, chat, site, and landing applications.

layers.name: Research
layers.description: Research artifacts, experiment scaffolding, and thesis materials that support and challenge the forecasting system.

layers.name: Operations
layers.description: Automation, workflow, deployment, and operator tooling used to run the repository and keep the system moving.

layers.name: Tests
layers.description: Verification coverage for the engine and product surfaces, including direct checks on data, graph, and workflow behavior.

layers.name: Misc
layers.description: Supporting files that do not fit neatly into the main engine, surface, research, or operations lanes.

tour.title: Start With The Thesis
tour.description: Read the repository from the outside in: the README and top-level Vaticinus briefs explain the product claim, why leak-free forecasting matters, and what this repo is trying to prove.

tour.title: Anchor The Method
tour.description: These files define the method and guardrails: doctrine, constitution, proof standards, and the future-map framing that keeps the project from drifting into hand-wavy AI prose.

tour.title: Follow The Core Engine
tour.description: The engine layer is where forecasting, scoring, world-graph compilation, and local orchestration actually happen. This is the technical heart of the repo.

tour.title: Inspect Data And Feeds
tour.description: These files show how evidence enters the system through feeds, world-state ingestion, and offload paths. They are the bridge between abstract theses and observable signals.

tour.title: See The Product Surfaces
tour.description: The repo has several outward-facing surfaces: a cockpit, a chat product, and public site layers. This step shows where the same underlying system gets rendered for users.

tour.title: Watch The Operator Workflows
tour.description: Operational files tie the method to real execution: agent workflows, run scripts, and ops notes for longer-running or more fragile forecasting jobs.

tour.title: Close With Verification
tour.description: The tests show what the repo considers important enough to lock down, especially around world-graph behavior, data collection, and forecasting control paths.
